headline: Data Centers Pay Grid Expansion Costs
short_summary: This bill requires data centers and other large energy users (25 MW or more) to pay for the costs of increasing electric generating capacity and related distribution infrastructure, preventing these costs from being passed to other customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Governor Abigail Spanberger, Delegate Destiny LeVere Bolling, Senator Louise Lucas, consumer advocates, environmental groups.
news_headline: Virginia Requires Data Centers to Pay for Power Lines.
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission ruled that data centers must pay the full cost for new transmission infrastructure they require, preventing these costs from falling on residential ratepayers. Governor Abigail Spanberger supported this decision, stating it will save residents hundreds of millions of dollars.

headline: Data Centers Must Report Water Use
short_summary: This legislation requires water suppliers to report the total volume of potable and reclaimed water provided to data centers to the State Water Control Board, enhancing transparency and aiding water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Elizabeth Guzman, Delegate Shelly Simonds, Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Potomac Conservancy, conservation groups, Virginia Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ).
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Data Center Water Use Tracking.
news_summary: Virginia's General Assembly passed SB 553, requiring water suppliers to report data centers' water usage to the State Water Control Board. This legislation aims to provide better data for informed decisions on water resources, especially as data center development continues to grow in the state.

headline: Data Center Siting Requires Noise Assessments
short_summary: This bill mandates site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential areas and schools for new high energy use data centers (100 MW or more) and allows localities to require assessments of impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Delegate Thomas, Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Virginia Conservation Network, community advocates, residents concerned about noise.
news_headline: Sterling Residents Report Excessive Data Center Noise, Pollution.
news_summary: Residents in Sterling, Virginia, are reporting excessive noise and fumes from data center generators, with one resident forced to leave his home due to 24-hour generator operation. This incident highlights growing community concerns about data center noise pollution and the need for stricter local regulations.
